scope: JO-GAP-004 history-row version-label oracle feasibility review
gherkinRequirement: Then two distinct revision rows (version 1 and version 2) are listed with timestamps and author admin

sourceFindings.finding: The history list renders Date, version note, Keep, Author, and Character Count columns. Each save-date link opens a preview using the history row's version_id. The list has no numeric article-version column; version_id is the history record key.
The pinned default com_content.article content-history options identify article.xml as the form and include version in hideFields, along with asset_id and checkout fields.
The preview loads the selected history record by version_id and prepares its version_data for rendering.
prepareData decodes version_data and applies hideFields before the preview layout receives the fields.
The preview renders the prepared field labels and values, so the default hideFields option prevents a Version row from being displayed.
The article form defines a readonly field named version with the Version label.
History storage serializes the full data object into version_data.
The data object includes every database table field, including the article version field, before the preview hideFields filter.
Article save increments the article version counter.

conclusion.reason: The history table has no numeric version label, and the default pinned com_content.article history configuration hides version from the linked preview. Therefore the stock UI cannot expose a row-associated visible version 1/2 assertion without changing application configuration or using a non-UI data channel.

reviewerDecisionRequested: Decide whether the Gherkin oracle should be revised to assert two distinct saved history snapshots plus the separately asserted article version increment, or whether a different source-backed observable oracle is intended. No Gherkin or human decision was changed by this review.
